chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about praying in the Euphrates and what is weaker than it from the rivers, while on the ship. He said, 'If you pray, it is good, and if you get off, it is good.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْفُرَاتِ: The Euphrates River, used here as a representative example of a large river.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying on a boat in a river according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of prayer (*Salah*) during river travel, specifically addressing the Furat River. By stating that both praying on the boat or disembarking to pray on the bank is 'good' (*hasan*), the Imam emphasizes that neither option is superior, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*taysir*) in travel. This ruling underscores the adaptability of ritual purity and posture requirements when navigating the variable conditions of waterways.
